relevance_note: Case series of four male Tangier disease patients with homozygous ABCA1 variants described individually: 'Genetic testing confirmed homozygous loss-of-function variants in ABCA1'.
method_note: Read the whole paper by hand; a short Python script in my scratch directory assembled the JSON from my readings and table-row segments copied from Tables 1 and 2 (output checked against the tables). Tables 1 and 2 have patients as columns; column headers are 'Patient #1^a', 'Patient #2^a', 'Patient #3', 'Patient #4' (^a = siblings). Labels follow the text form 'patient #1' etc. No supplementary material is in the converted file (detailed case presentations, Supplementary Table 1 and pedigrees are in an unavailable supplement). Table 2: abnormal values were taken only from cells printed bold, using the legend 'Bold values indicate that values outside the normal range'; non-bold values were not used to exclude anything (the legend does not define them as normal), except triglycerides for patient #2, which the text excludes by name. Table 1 '—' cells are undefined and treated as not reported. 'Normal' ophthalmological, echocardiography, carotid ultrasound and nerve conduction results were recorded as excluding only the abnormal investigation named, not corneal opacity, CAD or atherosclerosis. Low LDL is recorded as observed for all four from the group sentence 'standard lipid parameters were similar including ... low low-density lipoprotein (LDL) levels (7-50 mg/dL)', which covers the four patients' Table 2 values (37, 50, 31, 7), although these are not bold against the table's reference '<116'. Patients #1 and #2: 'Subjective hypesthesia' sits in the 'Peripheral neuropathy' row of Table 1 with normal nerve conduction, so the checklist item peripheral neuropathy was left not reported for them. Patient #3's 'Corneal dystrophy' was not mapped to the checklist item corneal opacity. Patient #3's foam-cell infiltration of the intestinal mucosa was mapped to intestinal mucosal lipid deposits using the paper's own definition of foam cells as cholesterol-laden macrophages. Orange tonsils: the text says '3 of 4 had a history of tonsillectomy due to reported orange-colored tonsils in 2 of them' without naming the 2; only patient #1 is 'Yes' in Table 1 (patient #2: tonsillectomy due to chronic tonsillitis; patient #4: 'Unclear'), so orange tonsils were recorded only for patient #1 (observed) and patient #3 (excluded, 'No'). Relatives: 'all relatives of patients #1 + 2 were heterozygous for the c.2418G > A' variant with reduced HDL, but their number and identities are not given in the main text, so they get no rows. The son of patient #3 gets a row (heterozygous c.679C > T); his lipid profile is only described as 'similar' to those relatives, so no phenotype was recorded for him. His inheritance is recorded as 'inherited paternal' under the v4 rule because the paper states that patient #3, a male patient and his parent, carries c.679C > T (homozygous). The 'Heterozygous relative (n = 1)' in Table 3 is not identified and was not assigned to anyone. The 'Uncle 55a' entry under family history of premature CVD for patients #1 and #2 was not given a row (not described as tested or affected with TD). Variant type was left not reported: the paper calls the variants 'loss-of-function' but names no class. Contradictions/inconsistencies: (1) patient #4's variant is 'c.5055del' in the Results and Table 2 but 'c.5055.del' in the Abstract and Discussion; (2) Methods say method-2 samples were from 'patients #2 and #3', the Results section says 'TD patients #1 and #3'; (3) patient #4's triglycerides are 468 mg/dL in Table 2 and 461 mg/dL in the NMR text (different assays); (4) patient #4 was diagnosed at 72 and is 'age 77' in the Discussion, recorded as age at last evaluation.
